stem: A patient has complete unilateral facial weakness including inability to wrinkle the forehead, close the eye and smile. Which lesion best explains this pattern?

options.label: A
options.explanation: This usually weakens the lower face with relative forehead sparing.

options.label: B
options.explanation: This weakens mastication and jaw movement rather than facial expression.

options.label: C
options.explanation: A lower motor lesion affects the ipsilateral upper and lower face, including forehead and eye closure.

options.label: D
options.explanation: This affects tongue movement and does not cause facial weakness.

options.label: E
options.explanation: This affects pharyngeal sensation and taste, not the muscles of facial expression.

context: Upper and lower facial weakness fits a lower motor neuron pattern. A facial nucleus or fascicle lesion in the pons can also produce this pattern, so forehead weakness alone does not exclude stroke.
